description: Step 5 of docs/the-delivery-loop.md: an independent review of one immutable commit. The mandate is one JSON object naming the repo, the branch and the mandate file the work was done under, with base optional; an unsaid base is the trunk the repository declares. The branch head is recorded and pinned under refs/sailor/reviews before anyone reads a line, together with the digests of the mandate and of docs/gates.md at that commit. The reviewer is handed a separate, locked checkout of exactly that commit and no author conversation. The verdict must name the pinned commit, say clean or findings, and list what it checked; it is written to the reviewed-commits collection keyed by branch and commit, which is what integrate-on-the-trunk reads. A branch that moves afterwards does not move the verdict: integration refuses a head that differs from the reviewed one. What this flow defends against: a different sailor found on PATH, since the brief names the sailor in service and its recorded sha256; a sailor in service that does not match that record, or that changes while the review is open; and a branch that moves after its head is pinned. What it does not defend against: whoever can already write to the directory of the sailor in service can replace that binary between its sha256 check and its execution; and a reviewer who closes the review step with the sailor on their own PATH instead of the one the brief names is not stopped, since a handed step is closed from outside the flow.
